blockers.description: docker compose --env-file .env.prod up -d redpanda on the Netcup VM prints 'variable is not set. Defaulting to a blank string.' for every one of the 7 vars in .env.prod (APP_DOMAIN, DB_NAME, DB_PASS, DB_JDBC_PARAMS, DB_HOST, DB_USER, IMAGE_TAG), even though the file exists, is 280 bytes / populated, and is in the same /root directory as docker-compose.prod.yml. Ruled out: wrong directory (confirmed via ls -la showing all 3 files together), missing file. Not yet ruled out: an `export KEY=VALUE` prefix on the .env.prod lines (Compose's .env parser does not understand `export`), or Compose v1 (`docker-compose`, hyphenated) vs v2 (`docker compose`, plugin) CLI mismatch. Diagnostic commands were sent to the human right before this pause; their output was not yet received when the session paused.
blockers.workaround: none yet -- next session should ask for `cut -d= -f1 .env.prod` and `docker compose version` output first if not already provided, then correct .env.prod's formatting (strip any `export ` prefix) or re-run with the correct Compose v2 command.

decisions.decision: DB_HOST in .env.prod must be Neon's DIRECT endpoint (ep-delicate-bird-b2lni8pr.c-6.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech), not the pooled -pooler one, despite INFRA-02's literal 'pooled' wording
decisions.rationale: Flyway takes a session-scoped advisory lock at boot; Neon's pooled endpoint runs PgBouncer in transaction mode, which does not preserve session-scoped state (Neon's own docs list this as unsupported). This is a single-instance app with a small HikariCP pool (max 5) -- no real need for the pooler's connection multiplexing.

decisions.decision: Expect 14 registry subjects when querying the production Schema Registry in Phase F, not the plan's stated 5
decisions.rationale: 05-04-PLAN.md and 04-VERIFICATION.md were written 2026-08-04; quick task 260811-s5e later expanded ActivityEvent from 6 to 14 types. build.gradle:606's registerSchemas task description already says 'Registers all 14 Avro schemas'. Treat the plan's '5' as stale text, verify against 14, and flag explicitly rather than silently forcing a match to either number.

decisions.decision: Added mem_limit: 3g to the app service in docker-compose.prod.yml and server.shutdown=graceful + spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase to application.properties, ahead of Task 1's own scope, before the tracer deploy started
decisions.rationale: The JVM has been container-aware since JDK 10 (reads cgroup memory limit for heap sizing) but only correctly if the container has an explicit limit -- app had none, so its 25%-of-container heap calculation was silently sizing off the host's full 8GB instead of a bounded slice, contradicting docker-compose.prod.yml's own comment about leaving headroom for Redpanda's 2G cap. Graceful shutdown closes a real gap where restart: unless-stopped could drop in-flight requests on every redeploy.
